chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ubayda ibn Abdullah ibn Ajlan al-Sakuni, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Sometimes I distribute something among my companions to maintain good relations with them by it, so how should I give to them?' He said, 'Give to them based on their emigration in the Religion, and their intellect, and their jurisprudence.'

key_terms.الْهِجْرَةِ: Emigration (metaphorical: leaving sin or moving towards Wilayah)

ai.seo_question: How should one distribute gifts or charity among companions according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that preferential treatment in distributing wealth or gifts should be meritocratic, grounded in religious devotion (*al-hijra*), intellectual capacity (*al-aql*), and jurisprudential knowledge (*al-fiqh*). This establishes a Shia framework for social hierarchy where spiritual and intellectual merit outweighs mere kinship or social status, reinforcing the concept of *awla bi al-nafs* (more deserving) in charitable distribution.
